pending_changes.text: GSA asked for comment, until March 30, 2026, on updating the [Financial Assistance](#term:financial-assistance) General Representations and Certifications in [SAM.gov](#term:sam-gov) to align with the Department of Justice guidance of July 29, 2025 on unlawful discrimination and with [Executive Order](#term:executive-order) 14173; the notice states no effective date [1866](#cite:1866).

variants.what: The [applicant organization](#term:applicant-organization) registers in SAM and renews yearly; a domestic organization gets a [CAGE code](#term:cage-code) and a foreign one an NCAGE code [4](#cite:4) [117](#cite:117).

[NSF](#term:nsf) requires an organisation to hold a valid and active SAM registration to use its systems and to keep it current while a proposal is pending or an award is active; [subrecipients](#term:subrecipient) need not register in SAM [156](#cite:156).
An active SAM registration is required before submitting to the DOE, DoD and [CDMRP](#term:cdmrp) notices read in this sweep [279](#cite:279) [336](#cite:336) [330](#cite:330).
Required before applying to every programme in this slice. [NIFA](#term:nifa) says to allow 4-6 weeks; NOAA Fisheries says 2 weeks or longer [421](#cite:421) [447](#cite:447).

[HHS](#term:hhs) research notices require an active System for Award Management registration, renewed at least annually, and the [UEI](#term:uei) issued with it; DOJ requires an active SAM.gov registration of every entity seeking its [grant](#term:grant) funding [507](#cite:507) [618](#cite:618).

[NEH](#term:neh), [NEA](#term:nea), [IMLS](#term:imls) and [IES](#term:ies) each require an active SAM.gov registration; NEH says a first registration may take several weeks, IES says up to 2 weeks plus 5 more if an [EIN](#term:ein) is needed, and IMLS says several weeks [644](#cite:644) [665](#cite:665) [677](#cite:677) [651](#cite:651).

name: SAM.gov entity registration
what: SAM.gov, run by the General Services Administration, is the federal registry in which an organisation must hold an active entity registration before it applies for federal financial assistance as a prime awardee [1897](#cite:1897) [1899](#cite:1899). Registration assigns the organisation its Unique Entity ID and, for a domestic organisation, a CAGE code [1898](#cite:1898) [784](#cite:784). An entity may choose a registration for financial assistance awards only, which asks for less than a registration for all awards [1898](#cite:1898). SAM.gov states that it is free to register and to keep a registration [1898](#cite:1898).
applies_when: Every organisation that applies to a federal agency for a grant or [cooperative agreement](#term:cooperative-agreement), unless the agency grants one of the exemptions in 2 [CFR](#term:cfr) 25.110 (national security, a foreign entity with an award under $25,000 performed outside the United States, or exigent circumstances) [1899](#cite:1899). A subrecipient needs only a Unique Entity ID, not a full registration [1900](#cite:1900). An individual applying on their own behalf through [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) does not register in SAM.gov [1896](#cite:1896).
steps: Create a SAM.gov user account, which is done through [Login.gov](#term:login-gov) [1897](#cite:1897).
Gather the data on the Entity Registration Checklist [1897](#cite:1897) [1898](#cite:1898).
Choose 'Register Entity' (not 'Get a Unique Entity ID') and choose the purpose: financial assistance awards only, or all awards [1897](#cite:1897) [1898](#cite:1898).

Enter the legal business name and physical address, which SAM.gov validates before it assigns the Unique Entity ID; if validation fails the entity can open a help ticket and attach documents [1898](#cite:1898) [1968](#cite:1968).

Enter Core Data: for a U.S. entity the Taxpayer Identification Number (validated), the CAGE code if one exists (otherwise one is assigned), and bank details for electronic funds transfer; a non-U.S. entity first obtains an NCAGE code [1898](#cite:1898).

Complete the Representations and Certifications; a financial-assistance registration includes the financial assistance certifications in Appendix I of the checklist (authority to apply, access to records, conflicts of interest, compliance with federal law, trafficking, drug-free workplace, civil rights) [1898](#cite:1898).
Name the points of contact: Accounts Receivable, Electronic Business and Government Business are mandatory [1898](#cite:1898).
Submit, and wait for the registration to become active [1897](#cite:1897).
time: SAM.gov says registration can take up to 10 business days to become active, and its checklist says to allow at least ten business days [1897](#cite:1897) [1898](#cite:1898). Grants.gov adds that it could take weeks or months if information is not available or verified [1895](#cite:1895). Agencies give their own, longer planning figures: [NIH](#term:nih) three weeks or more for first registration and two weeks for [renewal](#term:renewal); NSF at least 90 days before submission; [SAMHSA](#term:samhsa) at least six weeks before the due date; DOJ 30 days before a deadline; the Department of Education approximately 7 to 10 business days; CDMRP several weeks; [HRSA](#term:hrsa) two weeks for SAM and Grants.gov together [1909](#cite:1909) [161](#cite:161) [548](#cite:548) [619](#cite:619) [1928](#cite:1928) [1923](#cite:1923) [1925](#cite:1925).
cost: Free: SAM.gov states there is no charge to get a Unique Entity ID, to register or to maintain a registration [1898](#cite:1898). [ACF](#term:acf) and Grants.gov say the same [1961](#cite:1961) [1895](#cite:1895).
renewal: The registration must be renewed every 365 days to stay active [1897](#cite:1897). 2 CFR 25.200(b)(2) requires the registration to be current and active whenever the entity has an active award or an application under consideration [1899](#cite:1899). Under 2 CFR 25.205 an agency may not issue an award, or add funds to one, to an entity that is not in compliance [1899](#cite:1899). Grants.gov allows submission only while the SAM.gov registration is active [1965](#cite:1965). NSF notes that a lapsed registration takes longer to reactivate than one renewed while active [156](#cite:156). Registration records more than ten years past their expiration date are destroyed [1906](#cite:1906).
common_problems: DOJ states that failure to register in SAM.gov or Grants.gov in sufficient time is not accepted as a reason for a late application [619](#cite:619). Grants.gov tells the main contact to use the same email address in SAM.gov and Grants.gov, because the [Electronic Business Point of Contact](#term:ebiz-poc) named in SAM.gov controls the organisation's Grants.gov roles [1895](#cite:1895) [1965](#cite:1965). GSA tells entities under validation to make the name, address, start year and state of incorporation match the documents attached, and to answer emails from fsdsupport@gsa.gov [1968](#cite:1968). Recipients whose active federal awards and contracts total more than $10,000,000 must also report civil, criminal and administrative proceedings in SAM [548](#cite:548).

variants.what: The identifier an organization obtains through [SAM](#term:sam-gov) before doing business with the federal government; [NIH](#term:nih) uses it to count institutional limits such as the two-application limit on the DP5 [117](#cite:117) [104](#cite:104).
The identifier issued through SAM that each application must carry [325](#cite:325) [358](#cite:358).

name: Unique Entity Identifier (UEI)
what: The [Unique Entity Identifier](#term:uei) is the identifier SAM.gov assigns to an entity; 2 [CFR](#term:cfr) 25.400 defines it as the universal identifier assigned by SAM.gov to uniquely identify an entity [1899](#cite:1899). It replaced the DUNS number on April 4, 2022 [1969](#cite:1969) [1909](#cite:1909). An entity can get a UEI alone, without a full registration, by giving its legal business name and physical address; with a UEI only it cannot apply directly for federal awards [1897](#cite:1897).
applies_when: Every applicant includes its UEI in each application, and every [subrecipient](#term:subrecipient) must have one before a [subaward](#term:subaward) can be made [1899](#cite:1899) [1900](#cite:1900). A UEI alone is enough for an organisation that will only be a subrecipient; a prime applicant needs the full registration [1897](#cite:1897) [1900](#cite:1900). [NSF](#term:nsf) also requires named subrecipients to register in [Research.gov](#term:research-gov), and [SAMHSA](#term:samhsa) states that a UEI is required for recipients and all sub-recipients [156](#cite:156) [548](#cite:548).
steps: Sign in to SAM.gov with a [Login.gov](#term:login-gov) account [1897](#cite:1897).
Choose 'Get a Unique Entity ID' (UEI only) or 'Register Entity' (full registration, which also assigns the UEI) [1897](#cite:1897).
Enter the legal business name and physical address; SAM.gov validates them before assigning the identifier [1897](#cite:1897) [1898](#cite:1898).
Use the same UEI in every other registration ([Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), [eRA Commons](#term:era-commons), [eBRAP](#term:ebrap), Research.gov) [784](#cite:784) [358](#cite:358).
time: No page read gives a separate time for a UEI-only request; within a full registration the UEI is assigned once the name and address are validated [1898](#cite:1898). SAMHSA says activation and receipt of the UEI can take up to 10 business days [548](#cite:548).
cost: Free; SAM.gov states there is no charge to get a Unique Entity ID [1898](#cite:1898).
renewal: The UEI itself is not renewed; the registration that carries it is renewed every 365 days [1897](#cite:1897). For an entity with no active registration in the past ten years SAM.gov keeps an 'ID Assigned' record with only the UEI, legal name, physical address and assignment date [1906](#cite:1906).
common_problems: A recipient may not make a subaward to an organisation that has not obtained a UEI and given it to the recipient, and must tell potential subrecipients so [1900](#cite:1900). [CDMRP](#term:cdmrp) notes that Grants.gov registration takes significantly longer without a UEI [1923](#cite:1923).

pending_changes.text: The [Simpler.Grants.gov](#term:simpler-grants) roadmap gives 2027 as the stage at which Simpler.Grants.gov replaces legacy [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) and becomes the default experience [1919](#cite:1919).

variants.what: The organization registers in Grants.gov, where [NIH](#term:nih) applications are submitted and where all NIH funding opportunities are now posted [4](#cite:4) [121](#cite:121) [9](#cite:9).

Grants.gov is the alternative submission route; the authorised organisational representative signs and submits, and [NSF](#term:nsf) recommends starting at least five business days before a deadline [161](#cite:161). Collaborative proposals submitted separately by several organisations must use [Research.gov](#term:research-gov) [185](#cite:185).

The organisation needs a Grants.gov account whose representative holds the [AOR](#term:authorized-organization-representative) role; ONR says to allow at least 21 days for [SAM](#term:sam-gov) and Grants.gov together [336](#cite:336) [279](#cite:279).
The submission portal for [NIFA](#term:nifa), NOAA, EPA, NIST and USGS notices in this slice. NOAA Fisheries gives 2-4 weeks for registration [447](#cite:447) [409](#cite:409) [464](#cite:464).

Needed to submit applications to [AHRQ](#term:ahrq), [CDC](#term:cdc), FDA, [HRSA](#term:hrsa), [ACL](#term:acl) and [ACF](#term:acf), and to submit the [SF-424](#term:sf-424) that is step one of a DOJ application; an active SAM registration comes first [507](#cite:507) [619](#cite:619) [550](#cite:550).

All five funders in this slice take applications through Grants.gov; [IES](#term:ies) notes that only a user with the Authorized Organization Representative role can submit, and [NEH](#term:neh) [grants](#term:grant) no deadline extension for late registration [665](#cite:665) [644](#cite:644) [695](#cite:695) [677](#cite:677).

name: Grants.gov organisation registration
what: Grants.gov is the federal site where most agencies post funding opportunities and receive applications; an organisation registers there after SAM.gov, using its [UEI](#term:uei) [1895](#cite:1895). The person named in SAM.gov as [Electronic Business Point of Contact](#term:ebiz-poc) (EBiz POC) controls the organisation's Grants.gov roles, and at least one person must hold an Authorized Organization Representative (AOR) role to submit [1895](#cite:1895) [1916](#cite:1916). Applications are prepared and submitted in Workspace [1915](#cite:1915).
applies_when: Any organisation applying to an agency that takes applications through Grants.gov, which in this pack includes NIH, NSF (as an alternative to Research.gov), DOE, [CDMRP](#term:cdmrp) (full applications from extramural organisations), DOJ (the SF-424 step), HRSA, [SAMHSA](#term:samhsa), the Department of Education, NIFA and the [NEA](#term:nea) (Part 1) [1909](#cite:1909) [161](#cite:161) [279](#cite:279) [1923](#cite:1923) [619](#cite:619) [1925](#cite:1925) [548](#cite:548) [1928](#cite:1928) [1930](#cite:1930) [1934](#cite:1934).
steps: Complete SAM.gov registration, naming the main contact as Electronic Business Point of Contact and receiving the UEI [1895](#cite:1895).
Each user creates a [Login.gov](#term:login-gov) account, which Grants.gov requires of all users [1965](#cite:1965).

The EBiz POC registers on Grants.gov with the same email address as in SAM.gov, validates the address with a temporary code, and adds an organisation applicant profile with the UEI [1895](#cite:1895) [1965](#cite:1965).

The EBiz POC, who holds the Expanded AOR role automatically, assigns roles to colleagues in the Manage Profiles tab: Expanded AOR, Standard AOR, Workspace Manager or a custom role [1895](#cite:1895) [1916](#cite:1916).
A user with at least the Workspace Manager role creates a workspace for the opportunity; a user with an AOR role submits [1916](#cite:1916) [1915](#cite:1915).
time: Grants.gov gives no figure of its own beyond the SAM.gov wait; after SAM registration the Department of Education says it may be 24 to 48 hours before the information can be used in Grants.gov [1928](#cite:1928). NIH says to allow one business day or more, depending on how quickly the EBiz POC responds; DOE says an account can be created online in minutes; CDMRP says registration is processed immediately with a UEI [1909](#cite:1909) [279](#cite:279) [1923](#cite:1923).
cost: No fee is stated on the Grants.gov pages read; the page describes SAM.gov registration, the prerequisite, as free [1895](#cite:1895).
renewal: The registration itself is one-time, but submission depends on an active SAM.gov registration, renewed yearly [1895](#cite:1895) [1965](#cite:1965) [548](#cite:548). A Grants.gov account is deactivated automatically after 365 days of inactivity [1966](#cite:1966).
common_problems: Agencies ask for submission well ahead of the deadline because Grants.gov validates a package after receipt: DOJ urges at least 48 hours, SAMHSA 24-72 hours, and NSF at least five business days [619](#cite:619) [548](#cite:548) [161](#cite:161). The Department of Education extends a deadline only for a technical problem with the Grants.gov system that is confirmed by a Support Desk case number [1928](#cite:1928). The PDF forms in the Grants.gov forms repository are samples and cannot be submitted [1918](#cite:1918).

variants.what: The organization and each [PD/PI](#term:principal-investigator) hold [eRA Commons](#term:era-commons) accounts; the application image is viewed there, and [early stage investigator](#term:early-stage-investigator) status is computed from the investigator's profile [4](#cite:4) [121](#cite:121) [138](#cite:138).

NOAA applicants must register the organisation in eRA Commons before submitting in [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), and the Project Director or Principal Investigator needs an eRA Commons account linked on the [SF-424](#term:sf-424). This applies to applications submitted after January 1, 2024, when eRA replaced [Grants](#term:grant) Online; registration can take up to 4 weeks [447](#cite:447).

[AHRQ](#term:ahrq) and FDA research notices require the organization to register in eRA Commons with a [Signing Official](#term:authorized-organization-representative), and each principal investigator to hold an account [507](#cite:507) [564](#cite:564).

name: eRA Commons registration
what: eRA Commons is the system, run by [NIH](#term:nih)'s electronic Research Administration, in which an [applicant organisation](#term:applicant-organization) and its people hold accounts for applications, awards and reports [1911](#cite:1911) [1910](#cite:1910). The agencies eRA lists as supported are NIH, FDA, [CDC](#term:cdc), [SAMHSA](#term:samhsa), the National Institute of Food and Agriculture (USDA), the Department of Defense, the Uniformed Services University, AHRQ, the Department of Veterans Affairs and the Department of Commerce [1913](#cite:1913). eRA describes itself as the largest federal grants management system, with 1.3 million registered users [1913](#cite:1913).
applies_when: An organisation applying to NIH or to another agency that uses eRA registers once; every PD/PI, senior/key person and other significant contributor named on an application or award then needs a personal account [1909](#cite:1909) [1910](#cite:1910). SAMHSA does not accept an application if the organisation is not registered or lacks an active PI/PD account by the deadline [548](#cite:548).
steps: The organisation first holds an active [SAM.gov](#term:sam-gov) registration and [UEI](#term:uei), which eRA checks [1911](#cite:1911).

A Signing Official, a business official with authority to bind the organisation, opens the Register Organization link and states the purpose (NIH grant or contract, non-NIH grant or contract, or Other Transaction) [1911](#cite:1911) [1909](#cite:1909).

The Signing Official enters and verifies the UEI, enters institution details and contacts, and creates the first account for the Signing Official and optionally an Account Administrator [1911](#cite:1911).
The Signing Official answers the verification email within 8 days, or the request is cancelled; the temporary password that follows is valid for two days [1911](#cite:1911).
After approval the Signing Official or Account Administrator creates accounts for PD/PIs and other personnel [1910](#cite:1910) [548](#cite:548).
Each person who submits a Common Form links an [ORCID iD](#term:orcid) to the eRA Commons profile [31](#cite:31).
Users sign in with two-factor authentication through [Login.gov](#term:login-gov) or an InCommon federated account [1911](#cite:1911) [1914](#cite:1914).
time: NIH says to allow two weeks or more for eRA Commons registration, and six weeks or more for the whole set of registrations [1909](#cite:1909).
cost: No fee is stated on the eRA and NIH pages read [1911](#cite:1911) [1909](#cite:1909).
renewal: NIH describes registration as typically completed once and then maintained; no [renewal](#term:renewal) period for eRA Commons is stated, but the SAM.gov registration it depends on is renewed yearly [1909](#cite:1909).
common_problems: eRA requires PIs and key personnel to move to two-factor authentication 45 days after submitting a competing application or an [RPPR](#term:rppr) [1914](#cite:1914). NIH requires the same UEI in every registration [784](#cite:784).

variants.what: Every individual who submits a [biographical sketch](#term:biosketch) or [current and pending (other) support](#term:other-support) form to [NIH](#term:nih) obtains an [ORCID iD](#term:orcid) and links it to the [eRA Commons](#term:era-commons) account [31](#cite:31).

name: ORCID iD
what: An ORCID iD is a persistent identifier for a researcher, issued by ORCID, a global not-for-profit organisation sustained by fees from member organisations [1950](#cite:1950). NIH requires one of every person who submits a Common Form, linked to that person's eRA Commons account [31](#cite:31). DOE requires a persistent identifier field on notices and awards that include research and development, and its annual [Office of Science](#term:doe-office-of-science) notice asks for each senior/key person's ORCID iD if known [1944](#cite:1944) [279](#cite:279).
applies_when: At NIH: every individual who must submit a Biographical Sketch or Current and Pending (Other) Support Common Form, for due dates and for JIT, [RPPR](#term:rppr) and [prior approval](#term:prior-approval) submissions on or after January 25, 2026 [31](#cite:31). NIH notices also state that all PD/[PIs](#term:principal-investigator) must be registered with ORCID and have the iD linked to the eRA Commons profile [784](#cite:784).
steps: Register at orcid.org/register [1910](#cite:1910).
Link the ORCID iD to the eRA Commons personal profile before submission [31](#cite:31) [1910](#cite:1910).
time: No time is stated on the pages read [1950](#cite:1950).
cost: Free to the researcher: ORCID states that researchers create, edit and maintain an identifier and record free of charge [1950](#cite:1950).
renewal: None; the identifier is described as persistent [1950](#cite:1950).

variants.what: For due dates on or after January 25, 2026 senior/key personnel use the [Common Forms](#term:biosketch) and the [NIH](#term:nih) Biographical Sketch Supplement, completed in [SciENcv](#term:sciencv); since May 8, 2026 the system stops a submission that does not use them [31](#cite:31) [32](#cite:32).

name: Common Forms (Biographical Sketch; Current and Pending (Other) Support) prepared in SciENcv
what: The Common Forms are two government-wide disclosure forms, the Biographical Sketch and the [Current and Pending (Other) Support](#term:other-support) form, written by the National Science and Technology Council [Research Security](#term:research-security) Subcommittee to implement NSPM-33, with [NSF](#term:nsf) as steward [249](#cite:249). SciENcv, a researcher profile system run by NCBI at the National Library of Medicine, is the tool in which they are produced [1943](#cite:1943). NIH states that there is no blank template to complete outside SciENcv [1942](#cite:1942). Each agency adopts the forms on its own date [249](#cite:249).
applies_when: NSF: the biographical sketch and current and pending (other) support must be prepared in SciENcv under the [PAPPG](#term:pappg) in force (NSF 24-1) [257](#cite:257). NIH: required for due dates and for JIT, [RPPR](#term:rppr) and [prior approval](#term:prior-approval) submissions on or after January 25, 2026, together with the NIH Biographical Sketch Supplement; warnings only through May 7, 2026 and system errors that stop submission from May 8, 2026 [31](#cite:31) [1941](#cite:1941). DOE: for funding opportunities published on or after January 1, 2026, under FAL 2026-02 of December 3, 2025, for covered individuals at the applicant and at [subrecipients](#term:subrecipient) [1945](#cite:1945) [1944](#cite:1944). USDA: under the General Terms and Conditions effective December 31, 2025, at application and updated annually [1948](#cite:1948). NASA: NASA-specific forms in SciENcv, accepted alongside Word templates from June 25 to August 31, 2026 and alone from September 1, 2026 [1946](#cite:1946).
steps: Sign in to SciENcv with [eRA Commons](#term:era-commons), [ORCID](#term:orcid), [Login.gov](#term:login-gov), Google, Microsoft or academic institution credentials; NCBI no longer supports its own native logins [1980](#cite:1980) [1943](#cite:1943).
Complete the form the agency calls for: the Common Form, with the NIH Biographical Sketch Supplement for NIH, or the NASA-specific form for NASA [1942](#cite:1942) [1946](#cite:1946).
Certify the document; NSF requires each person to certify the current and pending (other) support information before submission [257](#cite:257).
Download the PDF that SciENcv produces and give it to the [applicant organisation](#term:applicant-organization) for the application or report [1942](#cite:1942) [279](#cite:279).
time: No time is stated on the pages read [1943](#cite:1943).
cost: No fee is stated on the pages read [1943](#cite:1943).
renewal: The forms are prepared afresh for each submission; USDA requires an update annually during the award, and NIH requires them with each RPPR [1948](#cite:1948) [31](#cite:31).
common_problems: An account holder may invite a delegate to manage SciENcv documents, but the person named certifies the content [1980](#cite:1980) [257](#cite:257). NIH's notice says failure to use the correct forms causes withdrawal of the application; its implementation page says that from May 8, 2026 the system stops any submission without compliant Common Forms [31](#cite:31) [1941](#cite:1941). NASA's forms are NASA-specific, so a form produced for another agency is not the NASA form [1946](#cite:1946).

pending_changes.text: [NSF](#term:nsf)'s certification took effect December 2, 2025, on a notice page marked updated November 24, 2025 [2014](#cite:2014). [NIH](#term:nih)'s notice of December 2, 2025 set May 25, 2026, after an earlier NIH notice setting January 25, 2026 was [rescinded](#term:rescission) on September 29, 2025 [33](#cite:33) [2016](#cite:2016) [127](#cite:127).

variants.what: For applications due on or after May 25, 2026, each senior/key person certifies [research security training](#term:research-security) completed within the 12 months before submission, through the [biographical sketch](#term:biosketch) in [SciENcv](#term:sciencv); the institution's authorized representative certifies as well [33](#cite:33).

Senior/key personnel on NSF proposals and awards must have completed research security training; the requirement took effect under Important Notice 149 on December 2, 2025, and the SECURE Center's condensed module satisfies it [247](#cite:247).

Covered individuals certify training completed within the 12 months before applying: at DOE mandatory after May 1, 2025 [310](#cite:310); at NASA effective August 5, 2026 for [PIs](#term:principal-investigator), Co-PIs and Co-Is at ten percent time or more [383](#cite:383).

name: Research security training certification
what: Section 10634 of the CHIPS and Science Act of 2022 (42 U.S.C. 19234) requires research security training for the people named on federal research and development applications [33](#cite:33) [2015](#cite:2015). Each funding agency has put the requirement into effect on its own date [2014](#cite:2014) [33](#cite:33) [383](#cite:383). In the agencies read, the individual certifies that the training was completed within the 12 months before submission, and the organisation's authorised representative certifies the same for all covered people [2014](#cite:2014) [33](#cite:33) [383](#cite:383).
applies_when: NSF: all proposals from December 2, 2025, for each senior/key person [2014](#cite:2014). NIH: applications for due dates on or after May 25, 2026, for senior/key personnel; NIH's systems enforce the certification for those due dates [33](#cite:33) [32](#cite:32). NASA: [grant](#term:grant) and [cooperative agreement](#term:cooperative-agreement) proposals from August 5, 2026, for all principal investigators and co-principal investigators, co-investigators spending 10% or more of their time on the award, and others a notice designates [383](#cite:383). DOE: [Financial Assistance](#term:financial-assistance) Letter 2025-02, dated October 8, 2024, covers covered individuals on applications for all research and development financial assistance awards; the landing page read gives no effective date [2019](#cite:2019). A university compliance page gives DOE's effective date as May 1, 2025 [2021](#cite:2021). USDA: an optional deviation to the department's General Terms and Conditions, effective June 3, 2026, updates terms on research security and malign foreign talent recruitment programmes [2020](#cite:2020). The Department of Defense announcement of January 8, 2026 lists research security measures and gives no date for a training certification [2084](#cite:2084). Read in the letter itself, DOE's FAL 2025-02 is effective upon issuance and makes the training requirement optional until May 1, 2025 and mandatory thereafter, for DOE and NNSA funding opportunities, [congressionally directed spending](#term:community-project-funding) projects and non-competitive agreements that include research and development; each covered individual certifies, and the applicant certifies for the covered individuals it employs [2107](#cite:2107). The PDF as returned gives the issue date as October 7, 2024 [2107](#cite:2107). USDA: section 10.6 of the General Terms and Conditions effective December 31, 2025 requires the recipient to certify that each individual it employs to work on the award has completed research security training, at the time of application or within the 12 months before work starts, and to recertify annually for the duration of the award [1948](#cite:1948). Deviation 2026-USDA-0001-F, effective June 3, 2026, restates the term for each covered individual and accepts training from NSF or the SECURE Center [2110](#cite:2110).
steps: Each covered person completes training that addresses cybersecurity, international collaboration, foreign interference, and the rules for proper use of funds, disclosure, conflict of commitment and conflict of interest [2014](#cite:2014) [33](#cite:33).

Accepted training is the set of four online modules developed by the agencies, or the one-hour condensed module from the NSF-funded SECURE Center, which can be taken online for a certificate or loaded into an institution's own learning system [33](#cite:33) [383](#cite:383) [2085](#cite:2085).

The person certifies completion: at NIH through the Biographical Sketch in SciENcv; NSF and NASA require each covered person to certify at proposal submission [33](#cite:33) [2014](#cite:2014) [383](#cite:383).

The [Authorized Organization Representative](#term:authorized-organization-representative) certifies, by signing the application, that every covered person has completed the training [33](#cite:33) [2014](#cite:2014) [383](#cite:383).
time: The SECURE Center describes its condensed module as one hour, replacing four one-hour modules [2085](#cite:2085).
cost: The SECURE Center page states no cost for its module [2085](#cite:2085).
renewal: Training must fall within the 12 months before each submission [2014](#cite:2014) [33](#cite:33) [383](#cite:383). NSF's training page says it recommends annual [renewal](#term:renewal) and that this is not a requirement [2015](#cite:2015).
common_problems: Dates on NSF's own pages differ: the notice page shows the training requirement effective December 2, 2025, while the training page says the notice was issued July 10, 2025 with updates effective October 10, 2025 [2014](#cite:2014) [2015](#cite:2015).

name: Training on other support disclosure
what: From October 1, 2025 recipient institutions train senior/key personnel on disclosing [other support](#term:other-support) and keep a written, enforced policy [128](#cite:128).

pending_changes.text: [NIH](#term:nih)'s list of initiatives in progress, last updated September 17, 2026, includes eliminating [data management and sharing plan](#term:data-management-plan) requirements on career development (K) awards; no effective date is given [2087](#cite:2087).

variants.what: Research that generates scientific data carries a DMS Plan, reviewed by programme staff rather than scored by peer reviewers; for due dates on or after May 25, 2026 the plan uses a new format page [124](#cite:124) [100](#cite:100).

name: Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan (NIH)
what: NIH's Data Management and Sharing Policy, in effect since January 25, 2023 (NOT-OD-21-013), applies to all NIH-funded research that generates scientific data, whatever the size of the award [124](#cite:124). The applicant submits a plan, NIH programme staff assess it, and the approved plan becomes a term and condition of the award [124](#cite:124).
applies_when: Research project applications, some [career development awards](#term:k-award) and research centres need a plan [124](#cite:124). Training (T), fellowship (F), construction (C06), conference (R13), resource (G) and SBIR/STTR [activity codes](#term:activity-code) do not [124](#cite:124).
steps: Write the plan in the 2026 DMS Plan format, required for all competing and non-competing awards under NOT-OD-26-046 [2029](#cite:2029).

Answer its seven items: maximum appropriate sharing; timing of sharing; how long data stay available; a justification of any limits, in 300 words at most; privacy protections for participant data; data types and repositories in a table, in 100 words at most; and the Genomic Data Sharing Policy where it applies [2029](#cite:2029).
Attach the plan in the "Other Plan(s)" field of the PHS 398 Research Plan and summarise data management costs in the budget justification [2029](#cite:2029).
Programme staff, not peer reviewers, assess the plan, and it must be approved before award [124](#cite:124) [2029](#cite:2029).

Share the data by the time of publication or, for other findings, by the end of the [period of performance](#term:budget-period), [no-cost extensions](#term:no-cost-extension) included [2029](#cite:2029).
renewal: Progress against the plan is reported in the annual [progress report](#term:rppr) [124](#cite:124).
common_problems: NIH may make data sharing an explicit condition of an award where a recipient does not comply [124](#cite:124).

pending_changes.text: The [NIH](#term:nih) Director said NIH will cap allowable publication costs starting in FY 2026 [2030](#cite:2030). A request for information of July 30, 2025 set out five options, from no support for publication costs to limits of $2,000, $3,000 or $6,000 per publication or 0.8% of direct costs or $20,000, whichever is greater, with January 1, 2026 as the intended effective date [2031](#cite:2031). No final policy was found in this sweep, and NIH's list of new initiatives, updated September 17, 2026, does not list one [2087](#cite:2087).

variants.what: An author accepted manuscript from NIH-funded work, accepted on or after July 1, 2025, is submitted to PubMed Central and made public without embargo on the official date of publication [34](#cite:34) [125](#cite:125).

name: NIH Public Access Policy compliance
what: Under the 2024 NIH Public Access Policy (NOT-OD-25-047), an author accepted manuscript from NIH-funded work that is accepted by a journal on or after July 1, 2025 is submitted to PubMed Central on acceptance and is public, without embargo, on the official date of publication [125](#cite:125). The 2024 policy replaces the 2008 policy [125](#cite:125). The 2022 OSTP memorandum had directed agencies to make federally funded publications freely available without embargo [2033](#cite:2033).
applies_when: The policy applies to journal manuscripts arising from NIH funding and accepted on or after July 1, 2025 [125](#cite:125).
steps: Submit the author accepted manuscript to PubMed Central when the journal accepts it [125](#cite:125).
Show compliance by the PubMed Central identifier (PMCID) of each paper [125](#cite:125).
Read the two [supplements](#term:supplement): NOT-OD-25-048 on publication costs and NOT-OD-25-049 on the government use licence and rights [125](#cite:125).
cost: Submission to PubMed Central carries no fee stated on the page read [125](#cite:125). Publication charges paid to journals are the subject of a pending NIH limit [2030](#cite:2030).

name: Unique Entity Identifier (UEI)
what: Every proposer provides a [UEI](#term:uei) with a new or [renewal](#term:renewal) proposal; [subrecipients](#term:subrecipient) named in a proposal also need one [156](#cite:156).
consolidation_notes: The same gate was recorded under two ids by earlier sweeps. The rules sweep wrote the full record under unique-entity-identifier; this record points to it (2026-10-04).

name: NSF ID
what: Each person who uses [NSF](#term:nsf) systems has one NSF ID, used as login and identity check [156](#cite:156).
consolidation_notes: The same gate was recorded under two ids by earlier sweeps. The rules sweep wrote the full record under research-gov; this record points to it (2026-10-04).

variants.what: [Research.gov](#term:research-gov) is [NSF](#term:nsf)'s own system for preparing, submitting and tracking proposals; the organisation registers there, and proposals sent through [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) are transferred to it [161](#cite:161).

name: Research.gov organisation registration and NSF ID
what: Research.gov is NSF's system for preparing and submitting proposals and for reports after award [161](#cite:161) [1955](#cite:1955). An organisation registers there, and each person holds one NSF ID, the identifier NSF assigns to a user [161](#cite:161) [156](#cite:156). A proposal may instead be submitted through Grants.gov, after which it passes to Research.gov for processing [161](#cite:161).
applies_when: Every organisation that proposes to NSF, and every [subrecipient](#term:subrecipient) named in a proposal, which must obtain a [UEI](#term:uei) and register in Research.gov without needing a [SAM registration](#term:sam-gov) [156](#cite:156).
steps: Hold an active and valid SAM registration and a UEI; NSF recommends starting at least 90 days before submission [161](#cite:161).
Register the organisation in Research.gov [161](#cite:161).
Each person obtains an NSF ID from a Research.gov account; a person may not have more than one [161](#cite:161) [156](#cite:156).

Sign in with multifactor authentication, using NSF credentials, [Login.gov](#term:login-gov) credentials or organisation-issued credentials through the InCommon Federation [1971](#cite:1971) [1972](#cite:1972).

Prepare and submit the proposal in Research.gov, or submit through Grants.gov with the [Authorized Organizational Representative](#term:authorized-organization-representative)'s signature [161](#cite:161).

NSF's Research.gov Account Management Guide (version 3.4, updated August 22, 2025) gives six steps for a person: confirm that no NSF account already exists; open Research.gov and select Register; enter registration information with a unique primary email address; set a password from the temporary credentials sent by email; set up a multifactor authentication method; add an organisational role, which reviewers and fellowship applicants do not need [2101](#cite:2101).
time: NSF gives no figure for Research.gov registration itself; it recommends beginning SAM registration at least 90 days before submission and, for Grants.gov submissions, starting at least five business days before a deadline [161](#cite:161). NSF's account management guide says an organisation must be registered in SAM.gov with a Unique Entity ID to appear in the system, and that completion of the SAM registration process may take up to one month [2101](#cite:2101).
cost: No fee is stated on the NSF pages read [161](#cite:161).
renewal: No [renewal](#term:renewal) of the Research.gov registration is stated; the SAM registration must stay current at all times while the organisation has an active award or a proposal under consideration [156](#cite:156).
common_problems: Multifactor authentication has been required at every Research.gov sign-in since October 27, 2024, and users with administrative or financial roles must use a phishing-resistant method [1972](#cite:1972) [1971](#cite:1971). A Login.gov address must match the primary email address of the NSF account [1972](#cite:1972). NSF's questions and answers on signing in, published January 31, 2025 and revised April 25, 2025, date the email rule from April 26, 2025: all users must verify that their NSF primary email address matches their Login.gov email address, and a changed primary email address must be verified within four hours or the account reverts to the last verified address [1972](#cite:1972). The guide says ongoing access to the primary email address is required for NSF communications and gives the help desk as 1-800-381-1532 and rgov@nsf.gov [2101](#cite:2101).

variants.what: [Office of Science](#term:doe-office-of-science) applicants generate biographical sketches in [SciENcv](#term:sciencv) [279](#cite:279); ROSES-2025 requires the SciENcv format for [PIs](#term:principal-investigator) and for Co-Is above 10% time [377](#cite:377).

name: SciENcv (biographical sketch and current and pending support)
what: [NSF](#term:nsf) requires the [biographical sketch](#term:biosketch) and the [current and pending (other) support](#term:other-support) document to be prepared in SciENcv [248](#cite:248). Government-wide Common Forms exist for both documents [249](#cite:249).
consolidation_notes: The same gate was recorded under two ids by earlier sweeps. The rules sweep wrote the full record under common-forms-sciencv; this record points to it (2026-10-04).

variants.what: A person who is a current party to a malign foreign talent recruitment programme may not be senior/key personnel on an [NSF](#term:nsf) proposal [156](#cite:156). From June 7, 2025 [PIs](#term:principal-investigator) and co-PIs on awards made on or after May 20, 2024 certify each year in [Research.gov](#term:research-gov) that they are not party to one [247](#cite:247).

name: Malign foreign talent recruitment programme (MFTRP) certification
what: A person who is a current party to a malign foreign talent recruitment programme may not serve as senior/key personnel on an NSF or [NIH](#term:nih) award [2014](#cite:2014) [31](#cite:31). The prohibition comes from section 10632 of the CHIPS and Science Act of 2022 (42 U.S.C. 19232) [31](#cite:31). Both the person and the institution certify [2014](#cite:2014) [31](#cite:31).
applies_when: NSF: the prohibition covers proposals and any award made after May 20, 2024 [2014](#cite:2014). NIH: the certifications are part of the [Common Forms](#term:biosketch) required for due dates on or after January 25, 2026, with a leniency period that ended May 7, 2026; from May 8, 2026 NIH's systems stop a submission that does not use compliant Common Forms [31](#cite:31) [129](#cite:129) [32](#cite:32). USDA's optional deviation effective June 3, 2026 updates its terms on malign foreign talent recruitment programmes [2020](#cite:2020).
steps: The individual certifies non-participation when signing the Biographical Sketch and [Current and Pending (Other) Support](#term:other-support) forms; at NIH each person, not a delegate, certifies in [SciENcv](#term:sciencv) [31](#cite:31) [247](#cite:247).
The institution certifies through the authorised representative's signature that senior/key personnel have been made aware of the requirement [31](#cite:31) [257](#cite:257).

After award, NSF principal investigators and co-principal investigators on awards made on or after May 20, 2024 certify each year in Research.gov; NIH senior/key personnel certify each year by a PDF uploaded to the [progress report](#term:rppr) [2014](#cite:2014) [31](#cite:31).
renewal: The post-award certification is annual at both agencies [2014](#cite:2014) [31](#cite:31). NSF's annual certification took effect June 7, 2025 [247](#cite:247).

variants.what: A code that the ONR and AFOSR announcements list among required registrations [334](#cite:334) [339](#cite:339).

name: CAGE code
what: A Commercial and Government Entity ([CAGE](#term:cage-code)) code is assigned to a domestic organisation as part of [SAM registration](#term:sam-gov) [784](#cite:784). A U.S. entity that has no CAGE code answers 'No' in the registration and one is assigned; the code is then validated [1898](#cite:1898).
applies_when: Any domestic organisation completing a SAM.gov registration, for [grants](#term:grant) as for contracts [784](#cite:784) [1898](#cite:1898).
steps: In SAM.gov Core Data, enter an existing CAGE code or select 'No' so that one is assigned [1898](#cite:1898).
If CAGE validation fails, follow the instructions in the email SAM.gov sends [1898](#cite:1898).
time: [CDMRP](#term:cdmrp) says SAM.gov registration takes several weeks, including 10-15 business days to process a CAGE code request or [UEI](#term:uei) [renewal](#term:renewal) [1923](#cite:1923).
cost: No separate charge is stated; SAM.gov registration, of which the CAGE code is part, is free [1898](#cite:1898).
renewal: No separate renewal rule was found on the pages read; the code is carried by the SAM.gov registration, which is renewed every 365 days [1897](#cite:1897).

variants.what: The [Office of Science](#term:doe-office-of-science) system for [pre-applications](#term:pre-application), [letters of intent](#term:letter-of-intent) and certain submissions, with a public award search [279](#cite:279) [366](#cite:366) [365](#cite:365).

name: PAMS (Portfolio Analysis and Management System, DOE Office of Science)
what: [PAMS](#term:doe-pams) is the Office of Science system in which letters of intent and pre-applications are submitted, alongside [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) for the application itself [279](#cite:279) [282](#cite:282). Its public site also offers a search of awards and [solicitations](#term:program-solicitation) [1922](#cite:1922).
applies_when: The [principal investigator](#term:principal-investigator), and anyone submitting on the PI's behalf, on an Office of Science application [279](#cite:279).
steps: A new user first logs in through DOE's OneID; international users are encouraged to use [Login.gov](#term:login-gov) [1922](#cite:1922).
The user creates the PAMS account and, if given a registration code, enters it from the Home screen [1922](#cite:1922).
Submit the letter of intent or pre-application in PAMS, and the application through Grants.gov [279](#cite:279).
time: The FY 2027 notice encourages registering at least a week in advance [279](#cite:279).
cost: No fee is stated on the pages read [1922](#cite:1922).
renewal: None stated on the pages read [1922](#cite:1922).

name: FedConnect
what: Named among the systems an [Office of Science](#term:doe-office-of-science) applicant registers with, and recommended by ARPA-E for notices of modifications [364](#cite:364) [301](#cite:301).

name: DOE eXCHANGE
what: DOE's platform for publishing funding opportunities and managing applications; ARPA-E's separate site was folded into it [306](#cite:306) [305](#cite:305).

variants.what: The portal for [CDMRP](#term:cdmrp) [pre-applications](#term:pre-application); investigators and organisations register there, and the organisation profile carries the [UEI](#term:uei) [358](#cite:358) [330](#cite:330).

name: eBRAP (Electronic Biomedical Research Application Portal)
what: [eBRAP](#term:ebrap) is the portal of the Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs; every funding opportunity requires a pre-application there [1923](#cite:1923). Extramural organisations then submit the full application through [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), while intramural Department of Defense organisations submit it through eBRAP [1923](#cite:1923). After submission the applicant checks the application in eBRAP during a verification period [1923](#cite:1923).
applies_when: [Principal investigators](#term:principal-investigator) and study personnel, business officials, account administrators and authorized organizational representatives of any organisation applying to CDMRP [358](#cite:358).
steps: The PI registers for an eBRAP account [1923](#cite:1923).
The organisation registers and enters its UEI from [SAM.gov](#term:sam-gov) in the organisation profile, required since April 4, 2022 [358](#cite:358).

The PI submits the pre-application in eBRAP: a [letter of intent](#term:letter-of-intent), which is not reviewed, or a pre-proposal, which is reviewed and leads to an invitation or not [1923](#cite:1923).
An extramural organisation submits the full application through Grants.gov [1923](#cite:1923).
The applicant reviews all components in eBRAP during the verification period [1923](#cite:1923).
time: CDMRP states that PI registration is processed immediately and organisation registration takes 1-2 days with a UEI [1923](#cite:1923).
cost: No fee is stated on the pages read [358](#cite:358).
renewal: None stated on the pages read [358](#cite:358).
common_problems: CDMRP states that there are no grace periods for deadlines [1923](#cite:1923). An eBRAP session expires after 15 minutes of inactivity [358](#cite:358).

variants.what: NASA's proposal system; every named team member must be registered and confirm participation before a proposal is submitted [388](#cite:388).

name: NSPIRES (NASA Solicitation and Proposal Integrated Review and Evaluation System)
what: [NSPIRES](#term:nspires) is NASA's pre-award system for [grant](#term:grant) proposals [1947](#cite:1947). Every organisation that intends to submit must be registered in it, and so must every individual with a role in the proposed work, who also confirms that role [1921](#cite:1921). Only the organisation's [Authorized Organizational Representative](#term:authorized-organization-representative) may submit a proposal through NSPIRES [1921](#cite:1921).
applies_when: All NASA grant and [cooperative agreement](#term:cooperative-agreement) proposers; the [principal investigator](#term:principal-investigator) must be a registered NSPIRES user even when the proposal is sent through [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) [389](#cite:389).
steps: The organisation registers in [SAM.gov](#term:sam-gov) with a [UEI](#term:uei); its [electronic business point of contact](#term:ebiz-poc) must be registered there [1921](#cite:1921).
The organisation registers in NSPIRES, and each individual registers and is affiliated with the organisation [1921](#cite:1921) [377](#cite:377).
Each team member confirms participation electronically on each proposal; a member with more than one affiliation chooses the institution through which funds flow [377](#cite:377).

Senior/key persons prepare the [biographical sketch](#term:biosketch) and [current and pending (other) support](#term:other-support) forms in [SciENcv](#term:sciencv), the only format NASA accepts from September 1, 2026 [1946](#cite:1946).
The Authorized Organizational Representative submits [1921](#cite:1921).
time: NASA's pages read give no time for NSPIRES registration; the Science Mission [Directorate](#term:nsf-directorate) asks proposers to register as soon as possible, and says a Grants.gov package for most ROSES-25 elements must be requested at least 30 days before the due date [389](#cite:389) [377](#cite:377).
cost: No fee is stated on the NASA pages read [1947](#cite:1947).
renewal: No [renewal](#term:renewal) rule is stated; a proposer who changes institution is told to obtain an NSPIRES affiliation with the new organisation at once [377](#cite:377).

name: ONR Submission Portal
what: Where ONR [white papers](#term:pre-application) are submitted unless an announcement says otherwise [336](#cite:336) [334](#cite:334).

name: Valid Eval application system (DOT University Transportation Centers)
what: The 2025 University Transportation Centers recompetition took applications through Valid Eval, an online application evaluation system, with a hard copy to follow by mail [493](#cite:493).

variants.what: The Department of Justice [grants](#term:grant) management system used by the Office of Justice Programs, the COPS Office and the Office on Violence Against Women; the full application is submitted there after the [SF-424](#term:sf-424) is filed in [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) [618](#cite:618) [619](#cite:619).

name: JustGrants (Justice Grants System)
what: [JustGrants](#term:justgrants) is the Department of Justice system in which the full application is submitted, after the SF-424 has gone through Grants.gov, and in which awards are managed [619](#cite:619). Its help desks serve applicants and recipients of the Office of Justice Programs, the COPS Office and the Office on Violence Against Women [1924](#cite:1924). Payment requests are made in Treasury's [ASAP](#term:asap-payments) system [1924](#cite:1924).
applies_when: Every applicant for DOJ grant funding, which must also hold an active [SAM.gov](#term:sam-gov) registration [618](#cite:618).
steps: Register or renew in SAM.gov; DOJ says to begin 30 days before any deadline [618](#cite:618).
Submit the SF-424, and the [SF-LLL](#term:lobbying-certification) where it applies, in Grants.gov by the Grants.gov deadline [619](#cite:619).
DOJ emails the address in section 8F of the SF-424 with instructions for creating a JustGrants account; DOJ expects the email within 24 hours [619](#cite:619).
The Entity Administrator, who manages which users may act for the applicant, sets up the organisation's users [619](#cite:619).
Complete and submit the full application in JustGrants by the JustGrants deadline; it may be recalled, edited and resubmitted before that deadline [619](#cite:619).
time: DOJ recommends completing the JustGrants steps at least 48 hours before the JustGrants deadline and submitting the SF-424 at least 48 hours before the Grants.gov deadline [619](#cite:619).
cost: No fee is stated on the pages read [619](#cite:619).
renewal: None stated for JustGrants; the SAM.gov registration is renewed every 12 months [619](#cite:619).
common_problems: [OJP](#term:office-of-justice-programs) considers a late application only where the applicant documents a technical failure of a government system and reports it within 24 hours of the deadline concerned; it does not accept late registration or problems with the applicant's own computers as reasons [619](#cite:619).

name: PCORI Connect
what: [PCORI](#term:pcori)'s application portal from Cycle 3 2026; a new or resubmitting applicant registers its organization and contact details before creating a login. PCORI Online remains for existing applicants and awardees [595](#cite:595).

variants.what: The [NEA](#term:nea) lists [Login.gov](#term:login-gov) with [SAM.gov](#term:sam-gov) and [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) as required registrations; [NEH](#term:neh) notes that a Login.gov account must be linked to Grants.gov [651](#cite:651) [644](#cite:644).

name: Login.gov account
what: Login.gov is a sign-in service provided by GSA's Technology Transformation Services that lets one account open many federal sites [1953](#cite:1953). It is the sign-in for SAM.gov, Grants.gov, [Simpler.Grants.gov](#term:simpler-grants), the [Federal Audit Clearinghouse](#term:federal-audit-clearinghouse), [iEdison](#term:iedison), [eGMS Reach](#term:egms-reach) at NEH and [IMLS](#term:imls), and USDA's [ezFedGrants](#term:ezfedgrants), and one of the accepted sign-ins for [eRA Commons](#term:era-commons), [Research.gov](#term:research-gov), [HRSA](#term:hrsa)'s [Electronic Handbooks](#term:hrsa-ehbs) and the Department of Education's [G6](#term:ed-g6) [1897](#cite:1897) [1965](#cite:1965) [1967](#cite:1967) [1881](#cite:1881) [1951](#cite:1951) [1932](#cite:1932) [1960](#cite:1960) [1929](#cite:1929) [1911](#cite:1911) [1971](#cite:1971) [1926](#cite:1926) [1963](#cite:1963). An account belongs to a person, not to an organisation; NEH states that shared accounts are not allowed [1932](#cite:1932).
applies_when: Every person who signs in to one of the systems above; [NIH](#term:nih) lists Login.gov for anyone with SAM, eRA Commons or Grants.gov accounts [1910](#cite:1910). Several systems require the Login.gov email address to match the address on the system account (Research.gov, eGMS Reach, iEdison, HRSA's Electronic Handbooks) [1972](#cite:1972) [1960](#cite:1960) [1951](#cite:1951) [1926](#cite:1926).
steps: Give an email address; Login.gov recommends a personal address the person will always be able to reach [1977](#cite:1977).
Set a password of at least 12 characters [1977](#cite:1977).
Choose an authentication method: face or touch unlock, security key, PIV/CAC, authentication app, text or voice message, or backup codes [1977](#cite:1977).
Where the agency system asks for it, verify identity by submitting pictures of a photo ID, or by showing the ID in person at a participating Postal Service location [1953](#cite:1953).
time: No time is stated on the Login.gov pages read [1977](#cite:1977).
cost: No statement of cost appears on the Login.gov pages read [1953](#cite:1953) [1977](#cite:1977).
renewal: No [renewal](#term:renewal) rule is stated on the Login.gov pages read; the systems behind it have their own inactivity rules, such as deactivation of a Grants.gov account after 365 days of inactivity and of [Payment Management System](#term:payment-management-system) access after 60 days without a login [1966](#cite:1966) [1973](#cite:1973).
common_problems: Systems differ in how strong a sign-in they demand: Research.gov requires a phishing-resistant method (face or touch unlock, or a security key) for Login.gov users and for anyone with an administrative or financial role, and HRSA requires an identity-verified account [1972](#cite:1972) [1971](#cite:1971) [1926](#cite:1926). Credentials from the former Census Bureau audit clearinghouse do not work at the GSA clearinghouse, which uses Login.gov [1881](#cite:1881).

variants.what: The second part of an [NEA](#term:nea) application is completed in the NEA Applicant Portal after Part 1 is filed through [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) [652](#cite:652) [650](#cite:650).

name: NEA Applicant Portal
what: An NEA application has two parts: Part 1, the Application for Federal Domestic Assistance/Short Organization Form, goes through Grants.gov, and Part 2, the [Grant](#term:grant) Application Form, is completed in the NEA's Applicant Portal [1934](#cite:1934). The NEA says the registrations that come first can take several weeks [1934](#cite:1934).
applies_when: Organisations applying to the NEA's Grants for Arts Projects; the same two-part pattern is recorded for other NEA programmes in the mechanics record nea-two-part-application [1934](#cite:1934).
steps: Register with [SAM](#term:sam-gov) and Grants.gov, and renew or verify existing registrations [1934](#cite:1934).
Submit Part 1 through Grants.gov [1934](#cite:1934).
Complete Part 2, the Grant Application Form, in the Applicant Portal [1934](#cite:1934).
time: The NEA says registration can take several weeks and estimates that drafting and submitting an application afterwards takes approximately 26 hours [1934](#cite:1934).
cost: No fee is stated on the page read [1934](#cite:1934).
renewal: None stated for the portal on the page read [1934](#cite:1934).

name: IES PRIMO application tracking (iesreview.ed.gov)
what: [IES](#term:ies) tracks applications in its PRIMO system at iesreview.ed.gov, where [letters of intent](#term:letter-of-intent) are also submitted [665](#cite:665) [663](#cite:663).

variants.what: [IMLS](#term:imls) award recipients manage and report on awards in [eGMS Reach](#term:egms-reach), where the award notification, approved budget and anonymised reviewer feedback are delivered [677](#cite:677).

name: IMLS eGMS Reach
what: eGMS Reach is the part of IMLS's [grants](#term:grant) management system, in use since October 1, 2019, that awardees and peer reviewers use [1933](#cite:1933) [1960](#cite:1960). Awardees view award information there and submit performance reports, interim and final financial reports, payment requests and change requests [1933](#cite:1933) [1960](#cite:1960).
applies_when: Every IMLS award recipient and peer reviewer; since January 20, 2023 each user needs a [Login.gov](#term:login-gov) account tied to the eGMS Reach primary email address [1960](#cite:1960).
steps: Create or use a Login.gov account under the eGMS Reach primary email address [1960](#cite:1960).
Sign in and use the Payments tab for payment requests and the report and change-request functions for the rest [1933](#cite:1933) [1960](#cite:1960).
time: No time is stated on the pages read [1960](#cite:1960).
cost: No fee is stated on the pages read [1960](#cite:1960).
renewal: None stated on the pages read [1960](#cite:1960).

variants.what: A foreign organization needs an [NCAGE code](#term:cage-code), in place of a CAGE code, to register in [SAM](#term:sam-gov); the [NIH](#term:nih) fellowship, career and training notices list it among the required registrations [784](#cite:784) [744](#cite:744).

name: NATO Commercial and Government Entity (NCAGE) code
what: A foreign organisation must obtain an NCAGE code, in place of a CAGE code, before it can register in SAM [784](#cite:784). SAM.gov's checklist tells a non-U.S. entity to request the code through the NCAGE Request Tool before starting its registration [1898](#cite:1898).
applies_when: Organisations outside the United States that apply as prime applicants and so need a full SAM.gov registration [784](#cite:784) [1898](#cite:1898).
steps: Request an NCAGE code through the NCAGE Request Tool [1898](#cite:1898).
Then begin the SAM.gov registration; bank details are optional for non-U.S. entities [1898](#cite:1898).
time: No time for the NCAGE request is stated on the pages read; NIH says the full set of registrations can take 6 weeks or more [784](#cite:784).
cost: No charge for the NCAGE code is stated on the pages read [1898](#cite:1898).
renewal: No [renewal](#term:renewal) rule was found on the pages read [1898](#cite:1898).

variants.what: ASSIST is [NIH](#term:nih)'s online system for preparing, submitting and tracking an application; it is one of three routes to [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) named in the fellowship notices, and it is where [loan repayment](#term:loan-repayment) applications are submitted [784](#cite:784) [763](#cite:763).

name: ASSIST (Application Submission System and Interface for Submission Tracking)
what: ASSIST is the eRA module for preparing an application on the [SF-424](#term:sf-424) forms, checking it and sending it through Grants.gov [548](#cite:548). [SAMHSA](#term:samhsa) strongly recommends it, with [Grants.gov Workspace](#term:grants-gov-workspace) as the other route [548](#cite:548). The eRA Service Desk supports ASSIST together with [eRA Commons](#term:era-commons) [1912](#cite:1912).
applies_when: Applicants to agencies that use eRA; the user signs in with the eRA Commons ID received at registration [548](#cite:548).
steps: Register the organisation and the people in eRA Commons [548](#cite:548).
Prepare the application in ASSIST and run its 'Validate Application' function [548](#cite:548).
Submit once errors are cleared; ASSIST routes the application to Grants.gov [548](#cite:548).
Follow the application under 'View Submission Status Details' in ASSIST [548](#cite:548).
time: No separate registration time: access follows from the eRA Commons account [548](#cite:548).
cost: No fee is stated on the pages read [548](#cite:548).
renewal: None stated on the pages read [548](#cite:548).

name: NRSA Payback Agreement (PHS 6031)
what: For a person's first 12 months of postdoctoral [NRSA](#term:nrsa) support, a signed [Payback](#term:service-obligation) Agreement Form (PHS 6031) must accompany the activation notice; people with an obligation file Annual Payback Activities Certification Forms (PHS 6031-1) until it is met [737](#cite:737) [736](#cite:736).

name: Research.gov GRFP application module
what: [GRFP](#term:grfp) applications are prepared and submitted only through the GRFP module of [Research.gov](#term:research-gov); materials sent any other way are not accepted [818](#cite:818).

name: NSF reference letter system in Research.gov
what: Reference writers for [GRFP](#term:grfp) submit letters through the [NSF](#term:nsf) reference letter system by a deadline earlier than the application deadline; for the mathematical sciences postdoctoral fellowship, letter authors need an NSF account in [Research.gov](#term:research-gov) [818](#cite:818) [840](#cite:840).

name: DOE WDTS online application system
what: SCGSR applications go into an online system run by ORAU, with two letters of support [894](#cite:894). The CCI page points applicants to an application portal to check status [900](#cite:900).

name: NDSEG application portal (Systems Plus)
what: NDSEG applicants register and apply at applyndseg.sysplus.com, run by Systems Plus Inc. for the DoD NDSEG Program Office [913](#cite:913).

name: USAJOBS application
what: NIST SURF students apply themselves through USAJOBS, with all documents as PDFs [979](#cite:979). USGS Mendenhall applicants submit through the USAJOBS link for the research opportunity, in PDF format [981](#cite:981).

name: Smithsonian SOLAA application system
what: Smithsonian fellowship applications are made in the SOLAA system [984](#cite:984).

variants.what: A person applying for an [NEH](#term:neh) award to individuals submits through [Grants.gov Workspace](#term:grants-gov-workspace) with a [Login.gov](#term:login-gov) account and an individual applicant profile; the notice read does not ask individuals for [SAM.gov](#term:sam-gov) registration [987](#cite:987). Individuals applying for Switzer fellowships also apply through [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) [1040](#cite:1040).

name: Grants.gov registration as an individual applicant
what: A person who applies on their own behalf adds an Individual Applicant profile to a Grants.gov account, either when registering or afterwards [1896](#cite:1896). An individual does not register with SAM.gov, does not manage roles and has no [Authorized Organization Representative](#term:authorized-organization-representative) [1896](#cite:1896).
applies_when: Only opportunities that an agency has opened to individuals; Grants.gov says individuals can apply for opportunities from certain federal agencies, and that most [grants](#term:grant) are for organisations [1896](#cite:1896) [1895](#cite:1895). None of the opportunities on Grants.gov is for personal [financial assistance](#term:financial-assistance), student loans or starting a small business [1896](#cite:1896).
steps: Create a Login.gov account and register on Grants.gov [1965](#cite:1965).
Add an Individual Applicant profile, at registration or after logging in [1896](#cite:1896).
Apply in Workspace, which Grants.gov describes as the standard way for organisations or individuals to apply [1915](#cite:1915).
time: No time is stated on the page read [1896](#cite:1896).
cost: No fee is stated on the page read [1896](#cite:1896).
renewal: A Grants.gov account is deactivated automatically after 365 days of inactivity [1966](#cite:1966).

variants.what: The fiscal year 2025 Fulbright-Hays dissertation notice required electronic submission in the Department's [G6](#term:ed-g6) system, with paper applications only by [prior written approval](#term:prior-approval) [1012](#cite:1012).

name: G6 (Department of Education grants and payments system, formerly G5)
what: G6, at g6.ed.gov, is the Department of Education's [grants](#term:grant) and financial management system; it replaced G5 (g5.gov) in a change completed on October 30, 2023 [1963](#cite:1963). Grantees draw down payments in it [1964](#cite:1964). Under the Department's common instructions of August 29, 2025, applications for [discretionary grants](#term:discretionary-grant) are submitted through [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), and the instructions do not mention G5 or G6 [1928](#cite:1928).
applies_when: Department of Education grantees, who draw down payments in G6 [1964](#cite:1964). The common instructions for applicants direct applications to Grants.gov and do not name G6 [1928](#cite:1928).
steps: Sign in at g6.ed.gov with [Login.gov](#term:login-gov) or with existing G5 credentials [1963](#cite:1963).
time: No time is stated on the pages read [1963](#cite:1963).
cost: No fee is stated on the pages read [1963](#cite:1963).
renewal: None stated on the pages read [1963](#cite:1963).

name: Smithsonian Online Academic Appointment System (SOLAA)
what: Applications to the Smithsonian Institution Fellowship Program are made in SOLAA [984](#cite:984).

name: IES letter of intent site
what: [IES](#term:ies) asks for a [letter of intent](#term:letter-of-intent) through its [peer review](#term:merit-review) site (iesreview.ed.gov) before the [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) application; for the FY 2027 training competitions it was due September 3, 2026 [995](#cite:995) [997](#cite:997).

variants.what: Awards in the first competition under the Education-Labor postsecondary partnership are issued on the Department of Labor's [GrantSolutions](#term:grantsolutions) platform [1015](#cite:1015).

name: GrantSolutions
what: GrantSolutions is a web-based [grants](#term:grant) management system; [ACF](#term:acf) and its recipients use it to manage discretionary and non-discretionary awards, and [CDC](#term:cdc) uses its Grants Management Module for CDC/ATSDR grants and [cooperative agreements](#term:cooperative-agreement) [1961](#cite:1961) [1962](#cite:1962). Recipients see the [Notice of Award](#term:notice-of-award) there and file post-award requests and programme reports [1961](#cite:1961). Its Online Data Collection system (OLDC) takes real property, financial and performance reports [1961](#cite:1961).
applies_when: Recipients of awards from agencies that manage awards in GrantSolutions; the pages read name ACF and CDC [1961](#cite:1961) [1962](#cite:1962).
steps: Complete a Recipient User Account Request form and have it signed by a supervisor or authorized official [1961](#cite:1961).
Email the form to help@grantsolutions.gov [1961](#cite:1961).
For OLDC reporting, submit the separate OLDC user access form [1961](#cite:1961).
time: No time is stated on the pages read [1961](#cite:1961).
cost: No fee is stated on the pages read [1961](#cite:1961).
renewal: None stated on the pages read [1961](#cite:1961).

variants.what: [HRSA](#term:hrsa)'s own system. Two-tier notices such as the Service Area Competition require a second submission in the [EHBs](#term:hrsa-ehbs) after [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov); look-alike designation applications, [progress reports](#term:rppr) and site verification are filed there; HRSA sends review results through it [1194](#cite:1194) [1150](#cite:1150) [1216](#cite:1216) [1152](#cite:1152).

name: HRSA Electronic Handbooks (EHBs)
what: The Electronic Handbooks are HRSA's own [grants](#term:grant) system, reached at grants.hrsa.gov [1927](#cite:1927). Members of an applicant or grantee organisation register once and are tied to the organisation's record [1927](#cite:1927). Since August 28, 2025 outside users sign in with an identity-verified [Login.gov](#term:login-gov) or ID.me account and two-factor authentication [1926](#cite:1926).
applies_when: Applicants, grantees, service providers, consultants and technical assistance users of HRSA programmes [1926](#cite:1926). HRSA's page on mandatory registrations before applying names [SAM](#term:sam-gov) and Grants.gov only [1925](#cite:1925).
steps: Create a Login.gov or ID.me account with the same email address as the EHBs account, and verify identity (photo ID, selfie, Social Security number) [1926](#cite:1926).
Go to grants.hrsa.gov, choose the user community and log in with Login.gov or ID.me [1927](#cite:1927).
Create the EHBs profile and choose a role: Authorizing Official, Business Official or Other [1927](#cite:1927).
Search for and select the organisation, and submit the request for the Primary Authorizing Official to approve [1927](#cite:1927).
time: No time for EHBs registration is stated; HRSA says SAM and Grants.gov together could take two weeks [1925](#cite:1925).
cost: No fee is stated on the HRSA pages read [1927](#cite:1927).
renewal: Registration is required only once [1927](#cite:1927).
common_problems: Login.gov identity verification accepts a state-issued driver's licence or ID, or a U.S. passport book; HRSA directs those without one to ID.me, which accepts a U.S. passport card or a non-U.S. passport [1926](#cite:1926).

variants.what: [SAMHSA](#term:samhsa) requires the organization to be registered in [eRA Commons](#term:era-commons) and the [project director](#term:principal-investigator) to hold an active eRA Commons PI/PD account by the deadline, or the application is not accepted. Its notices say to register at least six weeks before the deadline. Applications go through [eRA Commons ASSIST](#term:nih-assist) or [Grants.gov Workspace](#term:grants-gov-workspace) and must be validated by both systems [548](#cite:548) [1112](#cite:1112).

name: eRA Commons registration for SAMHSA applicants
what: SAMHSA requires three registrations before an application: [SAM.gov](#term:sam-gov), [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) and eRA Commons [548](#cite:548). The organisation's [Signing Official](#term:authorized-organization-representative) completes the one-time Register Institution form and then creates the account of the project director, whose eRA Commons username is entered on line 4 of the [SF-424](#term:sf-424) [548](#cite:548).
applies_when: Every SAMHSA [discretionary grant](#term:discretionary-grant) applicant, including non-profits that have never dealt with [NIH](#term:nih) [548](#cite:548).
steps: Start SAM.gov registration at least six weeks before the due date, as SAMHSA advises [548](#cite:548).
Register in Grants.gov; the person who submits must hold the Authorized Organization Representative role [548](#cite:548).
Name a Signing Official, who must hold the AOR role in Grants.gov and who submits the Register Institution form in eRA Commons [548](#cite:548).
After approval, the Signing Official creates the PI/PD account for the project director [548](#cite:548).
Submit through eRA ASSIST or Grants.gov Workspace so that the application is validated by both Grants.gov and eRA Commons by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on the due date [548](#cite:548).
time: SAMHSA gives no figure for eRA Commons itself; NIH says to allow two weeks or more [1909](#cite:1909). SAMHSA advises submitting 24-72 hours before the deadline [548](#cite:548).
cost: No fee is stated in the SAMHSA guide [548](#cite:548).
renewal: The eRA Commons registration is one-time; the SAM.gov account is kept active by updating it every 12 months [548](#cite:548).
common_problems: SAMHSA states that an application will not be accepted without the organisation's registration and an active PI/PD account by the deadline, and that no exceptions will be made [548](#cite:548).

variants.what: The [HHS](#term:hhs) system to which [HRSA](#term:hrsa) recipients submit the yearly [Federal Financial Report](#term:federal-financial-report) [1194](#cite:1194).

name: Payment Management System (PMS)
what: The [Payment Management System](#term:payment-management-system), run by the HHS Program Support Center, is a shared service that pays [grant](#term:grant) funds for federal agencies; recipients draw down funds in it and file the Federal Financial Report (SF-425) [1936](#cite:1936) [1961](#cite:1961). NASA also pays its recipients through it [1947](#cite:1947). For 2025 PMS reports more than $924 billion in payments [1936](#cite:1936).
applies_when: Recipients of awards from agencies that pay through PMS; the pages read name [ACF](#term:acf) and NASA, and [SAMHSA](#term:samhsa) and HRSA refer to it [1961](#cite:1961) [1947](#cite:1947) [548](#cite:548) [1927](#cite:1927).
steps: A new recipient sends the Program Support Center a Direct Deposit Sign-Up Form (SF 1199A) and a PMS access form [1961](#cite:1961).

Each user requests access online from the PMS login screen, choosing ID.me as the partner system and entering the payee number or PMS [Employer Identification Number](#term:ein) [1973](#cite:1973) [1974](#cite:1974).
The user's supervisor verifies the request and the Program Support Center reviews it [1973](#cite:1973).
time: Access and profile update requests are processed within four business days after PMS receives them [1973](#cite:1973).
cost: No fee is stated on the pages read [1936](#cite:1936).
renewal: A user must log in once every 60 days or PMS deactivates the access [1973](#cite:1973).
common_problems: The organisation name in the access request must match the [SAM.gov](#term:sam-gov) registration [1974](#cite:1974). NASA gives a payment request cut-off of 3:30 p.m. Eastern on the 23rd of each month [1947](#cite:1947).

variants.what: The system in which Collaborative Applicants and project applicants file [Continuum of Care](#term:continuum-of-care) applications and priority listings [1283](#cite:1283).

name: e-snaps (HUD's Continuum of Care application and grants management system)
what: [e-snaps](#term:e-snaps) is the electronic Continuum of Care Program application and [grants](#term:grant) management system used by HUD's Office of Special Needs Assistance Programs [1935](#cite:1935). Collaborative Applicants file the CoC consolidated application and the project priority listing in it, and project applicants file project applications [1935](#cite:1935).
applies_when: Collaborative Applicants and project applicants in a Continuum of Care competition [1935](#cite:1935).
steps: Each person creates an individual e-snaps user profile [1935](#cite:1935).
The person asks the administrator of the organisation's or the CoC's account for access to it [1935](#cite:1935).
The applicant determines its applicant type and completes the matching forms [1935](#cite:1935).
time: No time is stated on the page read [1935](#cite:1935).
cost: No fee is stated on the page read [1935](#cite:1935).
renewal: None stated on the page read [1935](#cite:1935).

variants.what: FEMA's [grants](#term:grant) system. For the Nonprofit Security Grant Program only the [State Administrative Agency](#term:state-administering-agency) uses it; a non-profit submits to the state agency instead [1320](#cite:1320).

name: FEMA Grants Outcomes (FEMA GO)
what: [FEMA GO](#term:fema-go) is FEMA's grants management system, used to apply for, track and manage grants [1957](#cite:1957). FEMA's FAQ lists Assistance to Firefighters Grants (with SAFER and Fire Prevention and Safety), Flood Mitigation Assistance and Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities on the system, with twelve more non-disaster programmes planned for fiscal year 2023 [1958](#cite:1958). It draws the organisation's record from [SAM.gov](#term:sam-gov) [1958](#cite:1958).
applies_when: Organisations that apply to FEMA directly in programmes on FEMA GO; the organisation needs an active SAM.gov registration with a [UEI](#term:uei) [1959](#cite:1959).
steps: Each user creates an account at go.fema.gov with an email address and completes registration from the emailed link [1959](#cite:1959).

The person listed in SAM.gov as [Electronic Business point of contact](#term:ebiz-poc) registers with the same email address and so becomes the primary [Authorized Organization Representative](#term:authorized-organization-representative) [1959](#cite:1959).
The primary AOR adds team members and gives each a role: AOR, Organization Member, Programmatic Member, Financial Member or Grant Writer [1959](#cite:1959).
An AOR signs and submits; a Grant Writer may draft and cannot submit [1959](#cite:1959).
time: No time is stated in the FEMA documents read [1959](#cite:1959).
cost: No fee is stated in the FEMA documents read [1959](#cite:1959).
renewal: None stated; access rests on the organisation's active SAM.gov registration [1959](#cite:1959).

name: GrantEase (Legal Services Corporation)
what: [LSC](#term:legal-services-corporation)'s online [grants](#term:grant) management system, through which every part of a Basic Field Grant application is submitted [1324](#cite:1324).

name: Runaway and Homeless Youth-Homeless Management Information System (RHY-HMIS)
what: The data system in which Runaway and Homeless Youth grantees enter data each quarter [1235](#cite:1235).

name: Homeless Management Information System (HMIS)
what: The local data system for homeless services.
